title: Bind mounts
idea: A bind mount maps a host file or folder into a container. Both see the same files, so an edit on one side appears on the other.

analogy.text: A shared network drive. Two people open the same file; neither holds a copy.
analogy.breaks: Either side can delete the file, and it is gone for both.

points: `--mount type=bind,source=HOST,target=CONTAINER` mounts a host path into the container.
Nothing is copied: the container reads and writes the host's real files.
A bind mount hides whatever the image already holds at that container path.
Add `readonly` to `--mount`, or `:ro` to the short `-v` form, for read-only use.

steps.caption: The mount makes the host folder appear at `/app`, in place of the image's own files.
The process reads `/app/server.js`, which is really the host's file.
You edit and save `server.js` on the host, as usual.
The container already sees the new file. Restart the process: no image rebuild.
Files the container writes under `/app` land in the host folder too.

code.caption: Run the API from your working folder, then try the short read-only form.

walk.text: Mount the current folder over `/app`. `source` is the host path, `target` the container path.
After editing `server.js` on the host, restart. The new code runs; no rebuild.
The short form is `-v HOST:CONTAINER`. The `:ro` suffix makes the mount read-only.

pitfalls: Mounting the project over `/app` hides the image's `node_modules`; install dependencies on the host too.
A typo in a `-v` host path creates an empty folder; `--mount` reports an error instead.
A bind mount depends on a host path, so keep deployed code in the image.

quiz.q: You bind-mount an empty host folder onto `/app`. What does the container see at `/app`?
options: The image's files, plus the empty folder
An empty folder; the image's files are hidden
The image's files, copied into the host folder
quiz.why: A bind mount shows the host path and hides what the image held there. Docker does not copy image files into it.

takeaway: A bind mount shares host files with a container and hides the image's copy.
